answer: Anchor each identity to one distinct rooftop solar installation, verified by satellite imagery: the panel array's basalt-dark surface, its ridge-line mounting angle and shadow signature form a fingerprint no software clone can fake. An attacker wanting ten identities must buy and install ten real arrays, each with its own grid meter, so cost scales linearly and visibly. Random re-imaging each epoch revokes vanished panels, and standing grows only while the installation keeps feeding the grid. Honest owners earn a durable horizon of trust; sybils face a hardware bill, not copy-paste.
